memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You will still be eating last year's harvest when you will have to move
it out to make room for the new'" - Lev 26:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a vivid picture of abundance. The storehouses would be so full of
last year's grain that the people would have to clear it out to make room
for the fresh harvest coming in. There would be more than enough, with
the old and the new overlapping.

This was part of God's covenant promise to Israel, and we should not turn
it into a guarantee of overflowing barns for every believer. But there is
a spiritual pattern here worth seeing: God's blessings are not static.
There is always something new coming in.

Dear friend, sometimes we cling so tightly to the "old harvest" — past
experiences, former ways, comfortable routines — that there is no room for
what God wants to give next. To receive the new, we sometimes have to
clear out the old.

Isaiah heard God say, forget the former things; do not dwell on the past.
See, I am doing a new thing! (Isa 43:18-19). Paul spoke of forgetting what
is behind and straining towards what is ahead (Phil 3:13).

This does not mean despising the past or being ungrateful for it. Last
year's harvest was real and good. It simply means holding it loosely
enough to receive what God has next.

Is there an old thing you are gripping so tightly that there is no room
for the new? God's mercies are new every morning (Lam 3:23). Make room.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I clinging to the old in a way that blocks the new?
2. What "former harvest" do I need to hold more loosely?
3. Where might God be bringing something new that I need room for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for past blessings, but keep me from clinging to them so
tightly that I miss what You have next. Give me open hands to receive Your
new mercies. Amen.
